definition: Gregarious means fond of company — craving the crowd and hating to be alone for long.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word gregarious. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know gregarious should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Gregarious since kindergarten, Rafa turned his paper route into a rolling block party, collecting company at every corner.
Companionable sits well below gregarious — it enjoys the one friend already there, with no urge to go find more.
Sociable comes closer but stops short of gregarious — a sociable guest enjoys the party she's at, while a gregarious one arranged it, packed the guest list, and is already planning the next.

Outgoing describes social confidence — the boldness to walk up to people you have never met and start the conversation yourself. Gregarious is about appetite rather than boldness: a gregarious person needs company around and seeks the group out. A shy person can crave the crowd yet never dare approach it.

Extroverted is the temperament word: energized by people rather than drained by them, recharging in company. Gregarious points at the behavior that follows — actively seeking the flock, joining every gathering, hating to be alone. Extroverted says where your energy comes from; gregarious says how hard you chase the crowd.

The bakery's new apprentice is gregarious to her bones: she joined the dawn crew's card game on day one, eats lunch wherever the most aprons are gathered, and volunteers for the county-fair booth just for the crowds.
Gregarious names an appetite for company: the gregarious person seeks the group out, joins it, and is fed by it.
It says nothing about warmth or charm — that is what separates it from affable and amiable — only that being alone is the one condition a gregarious soul can't stand for long.
Gregarious is about appetite for company, not warmth: a gregarious colleague fills her calendar with people.
Affable and amiable (both in this unit) describe how pleasant someone is once you're talking; gregarious describes how badly they wanted the crowd in the first place.
It also does honest work in biology — gregarious species live in herds and flocks.
